definition_en: to take action about something, or an agreement between two sides
core_image: 两人在桌边交换文件，然后握手成交
scene: 双方在桌边握了手，一笔买卖就这么定了。They shook hands to close the deal.
sceneCN: 这里 deal 指「交易」（第 1 个义项：双方达成的买卖或协议）；句意是他们握手成交。

senses.title: An agreement between two sides
senses.definition: an arrangement in business or politics that both sides accept
senses.definitionCN: 商业或政治中双方都接受的安排
senses.example: They shook hands to close the deal.
senses.exampleCN: 他们握手成交。
senses.why: A deal is a division that both sides agree to call fair.
senses.whyCN: 交易，是双方都愿意称之为公平的一种分配。

senses.title: To handle a matter
senses.definition: to take action about a problem or a person
senses.definitionCN: 对一个问题或一个人采取行动
senses.example: She knows how to deal with angry customers.
senses.exampleCN: 她知道怎样应对发火的顾客。
senses.why: Handling a problem is handing out the parts of it one by one.
senses.whyCN: 处理问题，就是把它的各部分一件件分派出去。

senses.title: A large amount
senses.definition: a great quantity, as in a great deal of time
senses.definitionCN: 很大的数量，如大量的时间
senses.example: It took a great deal of courage to speak.
senses.exampleCN: 开口需要极大的勇气。
senses.why: A share divided many times becomes an amount too large to count.
senses.whyCN: 一份被分了很多次，就成了数不清的量。

intro.en: Deal goes back to Old English dǣlan, to divide, and every sense still carries a share of that.
intro.cn: deal 可上溯到古英语 dǣlan（分开），每个义项里都还留着「分」的影子。

items.en: Dǣlan meant to divide something among people.
items.cn: dǣlan 意为把东西分给众人。

items.en: The noun named the portion each person received.
items.cn: 名词指每个人分到的那一份。

items.en: Deal came to mean doing business by exchanging shares.
items.cn: deal 开始指通过交换份额来做买卖。

items.en: Cards gave the word its sense of handing out what is held.
items.cn: 纸牌给了这个词「把手上的东西发出去」的意思。

items.en: A great deal of later turned the idea of shares into mere quantity.
items.cn: 后来 a great deal of 把「份额」变成了纯粹的数量。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the long e and final consonant, and the meaning group names other business and coping words.
note.cn: 形近组共享长元音 e 与词尾辅音，近义组则列出其他生意与应对的说法。

entries.definition: unable to hear
loved or expensive
the food eaten at one time
an agreement with better terms than usual
entries.definitionCN: 条件比寻常更合算的协议

entries.definition: an act of buying or selling
to manage a situation or a person
entries.definitionCN: 应付某种局面或某个人

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a thing broken into shares and end with a problem taken apart the same way.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从被分成几份的东西开始，落到以同样方式拆开的问题。

normal.en: To deal is to divide, whether goods or trouble.
normal.cn: deal 就是分，分货物，也分麻烦。

normal.en: Cards are dealt because a hand of cards is a share.
normal.cn: 牌要发出去，因为一手牌就是一份。

normal.en: A fair deal is one both sides can call dividing fairly.
normal.cn: 公平的交易，是双方都愿意称作分得公道。

normal.en: A great deal of time is time cut into too many pieces to count.
normal.cn: 大量的时间，是时间被切成了数不清的碎片。

normal.en: The word has never lost the idea of a hand passing something on.
normal.cn: 这个词始终没有丢掉「一只手把东西递过去」的意思。

abstract.en: Picture two hands meeting above a signed page.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手在签好字的纸上方相握。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of cards split into two even piles.
abstract.cn: 想象一副牌被分成两叠一样高。

abstract.en: Picture a problem laid out on a table in separate parts.
abstract.cn: 想象一个难题被拆成几块摊在桌上。

examples.en: They shook hands to close the deal.
examples.cn: 他们握手成交。

examples.en: She knows how to deal with angry customers.
examples.cn: 她知道怎样应对发火的顾客。

examples.en: It took a great deal of courage to speak.
examples.cn: 开口需要极大的勇气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deal 记成「地儿」：找对地方谈生意，分好各自的地儿，买卖就谈成了。

root: 源自古英语 dǣlan（分开、分配），与德语 teilen 同源；中古英语由「分得的一份」引申为买卖与协议，纸牌又带来「发牌」之义，后来 a great deal of 又把份额抽象成数量。

sensesIntro.en: From dividing a thing into shares, to the agreement about those shares, to a problem shared out and handled.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把东西分成份，到就这些份达成协议，再到把问题拆开应付。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands meeting over a page that divides something.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手在一张分配东西的纸上相握。

branches.en: The first sense is the agreement that makes the division fair.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是让这次分配显得公平的协议。

branches.en: The second applies the same dividing to a problem.
branches.cn: 第二个把同样的「分」用在问题上。

branches.en: The third keeps only the size of the share, not its fairness.
branches.cn: 第三个只留下份额的大小，不再管公平。

branches.en: A good negotiator and a good manager do the same thing.
branches.cn: 好的谈判者和好的管理者做的是同一件事。

branches.en: Handling a lot of work is dealing out a great deal of effort.
branches.cn: 应付大量工作，就是分发大量的力气。

intro.en: Deal is a productive verb, and its family grows through -er, -ing, and a set of phrasal patterns.
intro.cn: deal 是个能产词的动词，一族靠 -er、-ing 和一批短语长出来。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root stands behind deal; it is a native Germanic verb from Old English dǣlan.
latinIntro.cn: deal 背后没有拉丁词根，它是古英语 dǣlan 传下来的本族日耳曼动词。

a shop allowed to sell a brand

items.example: I will deal with the letters today.

definition_en: a person or business that buys and sells goods, or one who gives out cards
core_image: 车行里挂着钥匙、笑着迎人的销售员
scene: 车行老板把钥匙放在柜台上，报了一个价。The dealer offered a lower price.
sceneCN: 这里 dealer 指「经销商」（第 1 个义项：买卖某类商品的人或商号）；句意是经销商报了一个更低的价。

senses.title: A person who trades
senses.definition: someone whose business is buying and selling a kind of goods
senses.definitionCN: 以买卖某类商品为业的人
senses.example: The dealer offered a lower price.
senses.exampleCN: 经销商报了一个更低的价。
senses.why: The suffix -er turns the act of dealing into a person who lives by it.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -er 把「做买卖」这个动作，变成靠它生活的人。

senses.title: The one who gives out cards
senses.definition: the person who shares the cards among the players
senses.definitionCN: 在玩牌的人之间分牌的人
senses.example: The dealer turned over the first card.
senses.exampleCN: 发牌的人翻开第一张牌。
senses.why: The oldest sense of dealing is feeding cards to the table.
senses.whyCN: dealing 最老的意思，就是给牌桌递牌。

intro.en: Dealer is deal plus -er, so it names whoever divides or hands out.
intro.cn: dealer 是 deal 加 -er 构成，指负责分配或递出东西的人。

items.en: The base verb meant to divide among people.
items.cn: 词根动词意为在众人之间分配。

items.en: A dealer was simply one who handed out shares.
items.cn: dealer 最初只指分份的人。

items.en: Card players gave the word its lasting use at the table.
items.cn: 打牌的人让这个词在牌桌上固定下来。

items.en: Dealer also named a merchant of one particular goods.
items.cn: dealer 也开始指经营某一类商品的商人。

items.en: Car dealer, art dealer, and drug dealer fixed the pattern.
items.cn: car dealer、art dealer 与 drug dealer 固定了这一模式。

note.en: The look-alike group ends in -aler, and the meaning group names others who move goods.
note.cn: 形近组都以 -aler 结尾，近义组则列出其他转手货物的人。

entries.definition: to divide or do business
a person who makes others well
a person who guides a group
a person who trades in goods on a large scale
entries.definitionCN: 大规模做货物买卖的人

entries.definition: a person who buys and sells for a living
a firm that provides goods to others

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a hand of cards spread on a table and end with a row of cars under bright lights.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从摊在桌上的一手牌开始，落到灯下一排亮闪闪的车。

normal.en: A dealer is the one who decides how the shares fall.
normal.cn: 经销商是决定份额怎么落下的人。

normal.en: The card table gave the word its first steady job.
normal.cn: 牌桌给了这个词第一份稳定的工作。

normal.en: Add -er to dealing and you have put a person in the shop.
normal.cn: 给 dealing 加 -er，店里就多了一个人。

normal.en: A good dealer knows the goods better than the buyer does.
normal.cn: 好商人比买家更懂自己的货。

normal.en: The word carries no judgement; the goods decide that.
normal.cn: 这个词本身不带评判，是货物在决定评判。

abstract.en: Picture a fan of cards sliding across green cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象一把牌滑过绿绒桌面。

abstract.en: Picture keys hanging in rows behind a glass counter.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃柜台后一排排挂着的钥匙。

abstract.en: Picture two men talking quietly beside a parked car.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人在一辆停着的车旁低声交谈。

examples.en: The dealer offered a lower price.
examples.cn: 经销商报了一个更低的价。

examples.en: The dealer turned over the first card.
examples.cn: 发牌的人翻开第一张牌。

examples.en: They bought the van from a local dealer.
examples.cn: 他们从本地经销商那里买了那辆面包车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dealer 记成「递了」：deal 是分，-er 是人，把货一件件递出去的人就是经销商。

root: 由 deal（分配、交易）加施动后缀 -er 构成；中古英语时指分份的人，十六世纪因纸牌而固定为「发牌者」，十七世纪起又指经营某一类商品的商人。

sensesIntro.en: From the hand that shares out cards, to the shop that shares out goods.
sensesIntro.cn: 从分牌的那只手，到分发货物的那家店。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pushing a share of something across a counter.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把一份东西推过柜台。

branches.en: The first sense is a person whose living is the exchange itself.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是以交换本身为生的人。

branches.en: The second is the same hand, sharing cards instead of goods.
branches.cn: 第二个是同一只手，分的是牌而不是货。

branches.en: Both senses depend on giving each person a fair share.
branches.cn: 两个义项都靠给每个人一份公道。

branches.en: The card table is the older picture under the shop.
branches.cn: 牌桌是商店底下那幅更老的画。

branches.en: A dealer never keeps the whole deck.
branches.cn: 经销商从不把整副牌都留下。

intro.en: Dealer is a person noun built on deal, and its compounds are named by the goods it handles.
intro.cn: dealer 是建在 deal 上的人称名词，复合词则按经手的货物来命名。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root is involved; deal is native Germanic and -er is a Germanic agent ending.
latinIntro.cn: 不涉及拉丁词根：deal 是本族日耳曼词，-er 也是日耳曼语的施动后缀。

definition_zh: n. 院长；系主任；训导主任；座堂主任牧师
definition_en: the head of a college faculty, an officer in charge of students, or the priest who leads a cathedral
core_image: 一个原本只管十个人的组长，后来管起整座学院
scene: 院长把通知贴在办公室门上。The dean put a notice on the office door.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：dean 指学院院长；句意是院长把通知贴在办公室门上。

pos.zh: 院长；系主任；训导主任；座堂主任牧师

senses.title: Head of faculty
senses.definition: the teacher in charge of a college faculty
senses.definitionCN: 负责一个学院事务的教师
senses.example: The dean approved the new course.
senses.exampleCN: 院长批准了这门新课。
senses.why: A leader who began by counting ten people.
senses.whyCN: 一个从管十个人起步的负责人。

senses.title: Officer for students
senses.definition: the officer who looks after student discipline and welfare
senses.definitionCN: 负责学生纪律与福利的主任
senses.example: She went to the dean about her housing.
senses.exampleCN: 她为住宿问题去找训导主任。
senses.why: The same leader now watches over a group of young people.
senses.whyCN: 同一位负责人如今照看一群年轻人。

senses.title: Cathedral priest
senses.definition: the priest who heads the chapter of a cathedral
senses.definitionCN: 主持座堂牧师团的牧师
senses.example: The dean led the evening service.
senses.exampleCN: 座堂主任牧师主持了晚祷。
senses.why: A head of a chapter, as of a college.
senses.whyCN: 一个牧师团的首领，如同学院的首领。

intro.en: Dean comes from Latin decanus, the chief of a group of ten.
intro.cn: dean 源自拉丁语 decanus，即十人小组的组长。

items.en: Decem meant ten.
items.cn: decem 意为十。

items.en: Decanus was the chief of ten men.
items.cn: decanus 是十个人的首领。

items.en: Deien named the monk in charge of ten monks.
items.cn: deien 指管十名修士的修士。

items.en: Deen entered English as a church officer.
items.cn: 十三世纪 deen 以教会职务义进入英语。

items.en: Dean became the head of a cathedral chapter.
items.cn: 十六世纪 dean 成为座堂牧师团的首领。

items.en: Dean was used for the head of a college faculty.
items.cn: 十九世纪 dean 用于指大学学院院长。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dean- shape; the near-meaning group names other heads.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dean- 的字形；近义组都是「负责人」的说法。

normal.en: Decem means ten in Latin.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 decem 意为十。

normal.en: Decanus led a group of ten.
normal.cn: decanus 带领十人小组。

normal.en: A dean first led ten monks.
normal.cn: dean 最早带领十名修士。

normal.en: Then a dean led a cathedral.
normal.cn: 后来 dean 带领一座座堂。

normal.en: Now a dean leads a college.

examples.en: The dean welcomed us to the cathedral.
examples.cn: 座堂主任牧师欢迎我们来到座堂。

root: 拉丁语 decem（十）→ decanus（十人之长）→ 古法语 deien → 英语 dean

sensesIntro.en: One leader of ten, grown into a leader of many.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个十人之长，长成了众人之长。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chief of ten who now heads a whole college
core.cn: 核心意象：一个十人之长，如今主管整座学院

branches.en: Care of a group, whether students or clergy.
branches.cn: 照看一个群体，无论是学生还是牧师。

intro.en: Dean belongs to the ten family; the endings name offices and places.
intro.cn: dean 属于「十」这个词族；词尾表示职务与场所。

latinIntro.en: Latin decem means ten and caput means head.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 decem 意为十，caput 意为头。

definition_en: a state in which there is not enough of something that is needed
core_image: 货架空了一大半，想要的那样东西偏偏没有
scene: 证据太少，案子立不住。There was a dearth of evidence, so the case failed.
sceneCN: 第 3 个义项：dearth 指信息不足；句意是证据太少，案子立不住。

senses.title: Not enough supply
senses.definition: a shortage of goods such as food or water
senses.definitionCN: 食物、水等物资的短缺
senses.example: The war caused a dearth of grain.
senses.exampleCN: 战争造成了粮食短缺。
senses.why: An empty shelf where the goods should be.
senses.whyCN: 本该摆满货品的空货架。

senses.title: Hard to find
senses.definition: a lack of people or skills that are needed
senses.definitionCN: 所需人手或技能的缺乏
senses.example: There is a dearth of trained nurses.
senses.exampleCN: 受过训练的护士很缺。
senses.why: A post that nobody comes to fill.
senses.whyCN: 一个没人来填补的岗位。

senses.title: Too little information
senses.definition: a lack of facts, proof or news about something
senses.definitionCN: 关于某事的事实、证据或消息不足
senses.example: A dearth of evidence weakened the report.
senses.exampleCN: 证据不足削弱了这份报告。
senses.why: A page with only two lines written on it.
senses.whyCN: 一页只写了两行字的纸。

intro.en: Dearth is dear plus -th: the state of being dear, which came to mean scarce.
intro.cn: dearth 由 dear 加 -th 构成：本是「昂贵」的状态，后来变成「稀缺」。

items.en: Deore meant precious or costly.
items.cn: deore 意为珍贵或昂贵。

items.en: Derthe meant dearness, the state of being costly.
items.cn: derthe 意为昂贵，即代价高的状态。

items.en: The ending -th made nouns from adjectives.
items.cn: 词尾 -th 把形容词变成名词。

items.en: Costly goods were hard to get, so derthe came to mean scarcity.
items.cn: 昂贵的东西难买到，derthe 于是有了短缺义。

items.en: Dearth was used for famine and poor harvests.
items.cn: 十六世纪 dearth 用于饥荒与歉收。

items.en: Dearth is used for any lack, such as evidence.
items.cn: 二十世纪 dearth 用于任何缺乏，如证据不足。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -earth shape; the near-meaning group names kinds of not enough.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -earth 的字形；近义组都是「不够」的说法。

The ground, or the planet.
Costly, or much loved.

normalIntro.en: Dearth is dear plus -th: what is dear is hard to get.
normalIntro.cn: dearth 就是 dear 加 -th：昂贵的东西难买到。

normal.en: Dear once meant costly.
normal.cn: dear 曾经意为昂贵。

normal.en: The ending -th makes a state noun.
normal.cn: -th 把形容词变成状态名词。

normal.en: Dearth is the state of being dear.
normal.cn: dearth 就是昂贵的状态。

normal.en: Costly things are scarce things.

definition_en: a formal discussion in which two sides argue for opposing views
core_image: 两排人隔着长桌来回交锋
scene: 议会里两派人为预算争了一整个下午。The two sides will debate the budget again tomorrow.
sceneCN: 这里 debate 指「辩论」（第 1 个义项：正式的对立讨论）；句意是两派明天再辩预算。

senses.title: Formal argument between two sides
senses.definition: an organised discussion in which two sides defend opposite views
senses.definitionCN: 两种立场各持一方、有秩序地进行的讨论
senses.example: The two sides will debate the budget again tomorrow.
senses.exampleCN: 两派明天将再次就预算展开辩论。
senses.why: Two claims meet in public and each must answer the other.
senses.whyCN: 两种主张当众相遇，谁都得回答对方。

senses.title: A long argument among people
senses.definition: a serious argument among people who disagree
senses.definitionCN: 意见不同的人之间较真的争吵
senses.example: The plan caused a heated debate at the dinner table.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划在饭桌上引起了一场激烈的争论。
senses.why: Even without a chair or a rule book, people still take sides.
senses.whyCN: 就算没有主席和规则，人们照样会分成两边。

senses.title: To weigh a choice in the mind
senses.definition: to turn a choice over and over before deciding
senses.definitionCN: 在下决心之前反复掂量一个选择
senses.example: She debated whether to call him that night.
senses.exampleCN: 她那晚反复斟酌要不要打电话给他。
senses.why: A private argument is still a debate, held inside one head.
senses.whyCN: 一个人的内心争辩，也是一场辩论，只是发生在脑袋里。

intro.en: Debate came from Old French debatre, to fight or contend, built on Latin battuere, to beat.
intro.cn: debate 来自古法语 debatre（争斗），根源是拉丁语 battuere（击打）。

items.en: Battuere meant to beat or strike with a weapon.
items.cn: battuere 指用武器击打。

items.en: Debatre meant to struggle, with words as often as with arms.
items.cn: debatre 指争斗，用嘴和用兵器一样常见。

items.en: Debate entered English as both a quarrel and a formal argument.
items.cn: debate 进入英语时，既指争吵也指正式辩论。

items.en: Parliament gave the word its ordered, public sense.
items.cn: 议会赋予这个词有秩序、公开进行的含义。

items.en: Debate also means to weigh a private choice.
items.cn: 如今 debate 也指在心里掂量一个选择。

note.en: The look-alike group all carry a sharp middle sound, and the meaning group runs from calm talk to open dispute.
note.cn: 形近组中间都有一个清亮的音，近义组则从平和的商谈走到公开的争端。

entries.definition: money taken out of an account
money paid back after a purchase
money that you owe
to talk about something with others
to speak angrily because you disagree

entries.definition: a serious disagreement that lasts

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with two rows of speakers and end with one person arguing inside his own head.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从两排发言的人开始，落到一个人在自己脑子里争辩。

normal.en: A debate needs two sides, or it is only a speech.
normal.cn: 辩论得有两边，否则只是一场演讲。

normal.en: The stronger claim is the one that can answer back.
normal.cn: 更强的那个主张，是能回应对手的那个。

normal.en: Rules do not end the anger; they only keep it in chairs.
normal.cn: 规则不能消掉火气，只把火气按在椅子上。

normal.en: At dinner the debate begins over the salt and ends over politics.
normal.cn: 饭桌上的争论从盐罐开始，到政治结束。

normal.en: A mind that debates itself has two good speakers.
normal.cn: 在心里自我辩论的人，有两个好辩手。

abstract.en: Picture two hands raised at the same moment in a hall.
abstract.cn: 想象大厅里两只手在同一刻举起。

abstract.en: Picture a table where the same sentence is said twice, louder.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子上，同一句话被说了两遍，一遍比一遍响。

abstract.en: Picture a man walking home arguing with someone who is not there.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人走回家，一路和不在场的人争辩。

examples.en: The two sides will debate the budget again tomorrow.
examples.cn: 两派明天将再次就预算展开辩论。

examples.en: Her decision caused a heated debate among the staff.
examples.cn: 她的决定在员工中引起了激烈争论。

examples.en: He debated for a long time before answering.
examples.cn: 他斟酌了很久才回答。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 debate 记成「对掰」：de 是相对，bate 像 bat（球拍），两边各拿一块拍子来回对打，就是辩论。

root: 经古法语 debatre（争斗）进入英语，更早来自拉丁语 battuere（击打），所以辩论本来带着「交手」的意味。十四世纪入英语时兼指争吵与正式论辩，十六世纪议会用它指有秩序的公开讨论，现代又添了在心里反复权衡的意思。

sensesIntro.en: From two sides striking with words, to an argument at dinner, to a choice weighed alone.
sensesIntro.cn: 从两边用言语交手，到饭桌上的争吵，再到独自掂量一个选择。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two rows of people trading blows with words across a table.
core.cn: 核心意象：两排人隔着桌子，用言语来回交手。

branches.en: The first sense is the ordered contest, watched by a room.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是有秩序的较量，满屋的人看着。

branches.en: Take away the rules and the same contest becomes a quarrel.
branches.cn: 拿掉规则，同一场较量就成了争吵。

branches.en: The contest turns inward when one person holds both sides.
branches.cn: 当一个人同时站在两边，较量就转向了内心。

branches.en: Both are people disagreeing; only the setting has changed.
branches.cn: 两者都是人在意见相左，只是场合不同。

branches.en: A loud argument and a silent one share the same shape.
branches.cn: 大声的争吵和无声的争辩，形状是一样的。

intro.en: Debate has a short family: the person, the quality of being open to question, and a few fixed compounds.
intro.cn: debate 这一族很短：辩论的人、可争议的性质，还有几个固定搭配。

latinIntro.en: The Latin element is battuere, to beat; the modern word keeps the idea of verbal blows.

senses.definitionCN: 对帮助过自己的人怀有的亏欠之感
senses.example: She owes a debt to the teacher who believed in her.
senses.exampleCN: 她欠那位相信她的老师一份情。
senses.why: Help given freely still leaves a weight to be carried.
senses.whyCN: 别人白给的帮助，也会在心里留下一份要背的重量。

intro.en: Debt goes back to Latin debitum, a thing owed, from debere, to owe; the silent b is a scholar's gift.
intro.cn: debt 上溯到拉丁语 debitum（所欠之物），源于 debere（欠），不发音的 b 是学者的手笔。

items.en: Debitum meant a thing owed, built on debere, to owe.
items.cn: debitum 指所欠之物，来自 debere（欠）。

items.en: Old French dette dropped the b in both sound and spelling.
items.cn: 古法语 dette 在读和写上都去掉了 b。

items.en: English took dette from French and used it for money and favours.
items.cn: 英语从法语借来 dette，既指钱也指人情。

items.en: Scholars restored the b to show the Latin source; the sound stayed as it was.
items.cn: 学者把 b 加回去以显示拉丁来源，读音却没有变。

items.en: The silent b survives as a small monument to Latin.
items.cn: 这个不发音的 b 留了下来，成了拉丁语的一座小纪念碑。

note.en: The look-alike group hides letters that are not spoken, and the meaning group names what is owed.
note.cn: 形近组里都藏着不发音的字母，近义组则都在说「欠着的东西」。

entries.definition: an amount taken out of an account
entries.definitionCN: 从账户中划出的一笔钱

entries.definition: a feeling of not being sure
a short written form of department
money lent that must be returned
a duty that you must carry out
a debt recorded in accounts

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a line in a ledger and end with a favour that no money can clear.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从账本上的一行字开始，落到用钱还不清的那份情。

normal.en: A debt is a door left open until the last payment shuts it.
normal.cn: 债是一扇门，最后一笔还款才把它关上。

normal.en: Interest is time turned into money.
normal.cn: 利息就是把时间换成了钱。

normal.en: The b in debt is heard by no one and seen by everyone.
normal.cn: debt 里的 b 谁也听不见，却谁都看得见。

normal.en: Borrowing feels light in the hand and heavy at night.
normal.cn: 借钱时手上很轻，夜里却沉。

normal.en: Some debts are paid in visits, not in coins.
normal.cn: 有些债要靠探望来还，而不是靠钱。

abstract.en: Picture a red line in a ledger that no one has crossed out.
abstract.cn: 想象账本上一行没人划掉的红字。

abstract.en: Picture an empty purse and a calendar full of dates.
abstract.cn: 想象一只空钱包和一本写满日期的日历。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that helped you once, still held out.
abstract.cn: 想象一只曾帮过你的手，还伸在那里。

examples.en: It took him six years to pay off the debt.
examples.cn: 他花了六年才还清这笔债。

examples.en: The company is deep in debt after two bad years.
examples.cn: 公司经历两个坏年头后债台高筑。

examples.en: She owes a debt to the doctor who saved her son.
examples.cn: 她欠那位救了她儿子的医生一份情。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 debt 记成「待」：b 不发音像躲起来，剩下 det 念起来像「待」，欠了钱就得一直待着等还。

root: 源自拉丁语 debitum（所欠之物），动词 debere 意为「欠」。古法语作 dette，把 b 从读音和拼写里都去掉了；英语十三世纪借入，十六世纪学者又按拉丁原形把 b 补回拼写，读音仍旧不发，于是留下这个看得见听不见的字母。

sensesIntro.en: From a sum of money owed, to the weight of a kindness that cannot be counted.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一笔要还的钱，到一份数不清的人情。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an uncrossed line of red ink in a ledger.
core.cn: 核心意象：账本上一行没有被划掉的红字。

branches.en: The first sense is the sum borrowed and not yet returned.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是借来还没还的那笔钱。

branches.en: Kindness borrows the same shape, though no ledger records it.
branches.cn: 好意也长成同样的形状，只是没有账本记着。

branches.en: Money and gratitude both leave a person owing something.
branches.cn: 钱和恩情，都让人心里欠着点什么。

branches.en: Both senses explain why the word can be paid and also felt.
branches.cn: 两个义项解释了为什么这个词既能「还」，也能「感到」。

branches.en: The second sense lasts longer, because it has no final payment.
branches.cn: 第二个义项更长久，因为它没有最后一次结清。

intro.en: Debt forms a compact family around owing: the person who owes, the state of owing, and the relief of being free.
intro.cn: debt 这一族都围绕「欠」：欠的人、欠的状态，以及无债的轻松。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is debere, to owe; its participle debitum gives the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 debere（欠），其分词 debitum 演变成英语名词。

items.example: The debt was cleared last month.
The debtor asked for more time.
items.exampleCN: 债务人请求宽限一些时间。

items.example: I am indebted to you for your help.
items.exampleCN: 你的帮助让我十分感激。
他们四十岁时已无债一身轻。
不欠债的农夫睡得踏实。

items.meaning: a situation where debts cannot be paid
items.example: The country faced a debt crisis.
items.exampleCN: 这个国家面临债务危机。

items.meaning: the cancelling or easing of debts
items.example: The bank offered debt relief to farmers.
items.exampleCN: 银行给农民提供了债务减免。

items.meaning: a person paid to recover debts

definition_en: a period of ten years
core_image: 日历上翻过的十本厚册
scene: 老照片记下了这个街区几十年的变化。The shop has stood on this corner for a decade.
sceneCN: 这里 decade 指「十年」（第 1 个义项：十个年头）；句意是这家店在这个街角开了十年。

senses.title: Any period of ten years
senses.definition: a length of ten years counted from any starting point
senses.definitionCN: 从任意一点起算的十个年头
senses.example: The shop has stood on this corner for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店在这个街角已经开了十年。
senses.why: Ten fingers, ten years: counting by tens is older than any calendar.
senses.whyCN: 十根手指、十个年头，按十计数比历法还要古老。

senses.title: A named ten-year span
senses.definition: one of the ten-year blocks used to talk about history
senses.definitionCN: 谈论历史时用来切分时间的一个十年段
senses.example: The music of that decade still sounds fresh.
senses.exampleCN: 那个年代的音乐如今听着仍然新鲜。
senses.why: History is easier to hold when it is cut into named blocks.
senses.whyCN: 历史切成有名字的块，才更容易被人握住。

intro.en: Decade came from Greek dekas, a group of ten, through Latin decas and French décade.
intro.cn: decade 经拉丁语 decas 与法语 décade，上溯到希腊语 dekas（一组十个）。

items.en: Dekas meant a set of ten, from deka, the number ten.
items.cn: dekas 指一组十个，来自 deka（十）。

items.en: Decas kept the Greek sense of a group of ten things.
items.cn: decas 保留了希腊语「十个一组」的意思。

items.en: Décade was used for a period of ten days or ten years.
items.cn: décade 曾用来指十天或十年。

items.en: English settled decade on ten years.
items.cn: 英语把 decade 固定为「十年」。

items.en: The word now also labels cultural periods such as the nineties.
items.cn: 如今这个词也用来称呼九十年代这样的文化时期。

note.en: The look-alike group begins with the same dec- letters, and the meaning group measures time in different lengths.
note.cn: 形近组都以 dec- 开头，近义组则用不同长度来量时间。

entries.definition: to turn a code into ordinary language
a unit for measuring the loudness of sound
a flat shape with ten straight sides
entries.definitionCN: 有十条直边的平面图形

entries.definition: a period of one hundred years
a long period with a shared character
entries.definitionCN: 具有共同特征的漫长时期

entries.definition: the length of time something lasts

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with ten fingers and end with a block of history that has a name.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从十根手指开始，落到一段有了名字的历史。

normal.en: A decade is long enough to change a street and short enough to remember.
normal.cn: 十年长到能改一条街，又短到还记得清。

normal.en: Count ten new years and a decade has passed without a sound.
normal.cn: 数过十个新年，十年就悄没声地过去了。

normal.en: Photographs are the only scales that weigh a decade.
normal.cn: 照片是唯一能称出十年重量的秤。

normal.en: A child of one decade becomes the parent of the next.
normal.cn: 这个十年的孩子，成了下个十年的父母。

normal.en: Dec- at the front means ten, as in ten-sided shapes and ten-year spans.
normal.cn: 开头的 dec- 表示十，十边形和十年都是它。

abstract.en: Picture ten thick calendars stacked in one corner.
abstract.cn: 想象十本厚日历堆在一个角落。

abstract.en: Picture the same corner photographed once every ten years.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个街角,每十年被拍下一次。

abstract.en: Picture a child and then the same face with grey hair.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子，然后是同一张脸生出白发。

examples.en: The shop has stood on this corner for a decade.
examples.cn: 这家店在这个街角已经开了十年。

examples.en: Prices have doubled over the past decade.
examples.cn: 过去十年里物价翻了一倍。

examples.en: Each decade of his life brought a new city.
examples.cn: 他人生中的每一个十年都带来一座新城市。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 decade 记成「得开的」：de 加 cade 像「得开的」，十年一过，旧日子就得让开，新的日子开进来。

root: 源自希腊语 dekas（一组十个），经拉丁语 decas 与法语 décade 进入英语。法语里它一度兼指十天与十年，十七世纪英语才把它固定为十年，现代又用来指称九十年代这样有共同风格的历史时段。

sensesIntro.en: From any count of ten years to a block of history that carries a name.
sensesIntro.cn: 从任意的十个年头，到一段有了名字的历史。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ten thick calendars stacked in one corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：十本厚厚的日历堆在角落里。

branches.en: The first sense is a plain count of ten years from any point.
branches.cn: 第一个义项只是从任意一点数满十年。

branches.en: Once the ten years are shared by many, they become a named block.
branches.cn: 当这十年被许多人共同经历，就成了有名字的一段。

branches.en: The same length of time, one measured and one remembered.
branches.cn: 同样长的时间，一个用来量，一个用来回忆。

branches.en: Both senses depend on counting by tens, an old habit of the hand.
branches.cn: 两个义项都靠按十计数，那是手上传下来的老习惯。

branches.en: Naming a decade is a way of saying that a change was shared.
branches.cn: 给十年命名，其实是在说这场变化人人都经历过。

intro.en: Decade belongs to the dec- family, where the number ten is spelled into shapes, spans and measures.
intro.cn: decade 属于 dec- 这一族，数字十被写进形状、时段与度量里。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is decem, ten, with decimus for tenth; Greek deka gave the same idea.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 decem（十），decimus 表示第十；希腊语 deka 意思相同。

items.example: A decade passed before they met again.
items.exampleCN: 过了十年他们才又见面。
这份报告研究十年尺度的变化。

items.example: The decennial census begins in spring.
items.exampleCN: 每十年一次的人口普查春天开始。
他们完成了一项长达十年的研究。

items.example: A decades-old tree shades the yard.
items.exampleCN: 一棵几十年的老树遮着院子。

items.meaning: a formal word for ten years
items.example: The charter is renewed each decennium.
items.exampleCN: 这份章程每十年续签一次。

items.example: The map changed decade by decade.

latinEntries.example: Decem is the Latin word for ten.
Decimus marks the tenth place in a list.
latinEntries.exampleCN: decimus 表示列表中的第十位。

definition_zh: v. 斩首；砍头；（比喻）清除领导层
definition_en: to cut off the head of a person or animal, or to remove the leaders of a group
core_image: 一把刀落下，头与身体分开
scene: 国王在广场上被斩首。The king was decapitated in the square.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：decapitate 指斩首；句意是国王在广场上被斩首。

senses.title: Cut off the head
senses.definition: to cut the head off a person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 把人或动物的头砍下
senses.example: The prisoner was decapitated at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 囚犯在黎明时被斩首。
senses.why: A blade falling and a head parting from a body.
senses.whyCN: 一把刀落下，头与身体分开。

senses.title: Remove the leaders
senses.definition: to destroy the leadership of a group or organisation
senses.definitionCN: 摧毁一个团体或组织的领导层
senses.example: The strike decapitated the company.
senses.exampleCN: 那次打击使公司失去了领导层。
senses.why: A tree whose top branch is cut away.
senses.whyCN: 一棵被砍掉顶枝的树。

intro.en: Decapitate is de- off plus caput head: to take the head off.
intro.cn: decapitate 由 de-（去掉）加 caput（头）构成：把头去掉。

items.en: Caput meant head.
items.cn: caput 意为头。

items.en: The prefix de- meant off or away.
items.cn: 前缀 de- 意为离开或去掉。

items.en: Decapitare meant to take the head off.
items.cn: decapitare 意为把头去掉。

items.en: Decapitate entered English for execution by beheading.
items.cn: 十七世纪 decapitate 以斩首处决义进入英语。

items.en: Decapitate was used in histories of revolution.
items.cn: 十九世纪 decapitate 用于革命史叙述。

items.en: Decapitate gained a figurative sense of removing leaders.
items.cn: 二十世纪 decapitate 获得「清除领导层」的比喻义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares capit-; the near-meaning group names ways of killing or removing.
note.cn: 形近组共享 capit-；近义组都是「处死或去掉」的说法。

entries.definition: The chief city, or a crime punished by death.
The leader of a team or a ship.
The act of cutting off a head.
Shaped like a head.
To cut off the head of someone.
To kill someone as a legal punishment.
To kill with a falling blade.
To destroy a large part of something.

normalIntro.en: Decapitate is de- off plus caput head: off with the head.
normalIntro.cn: decapitate 就是 de-（去掉）加 caput（头）：把头去掉。

normal.en: Caput means head in Latin.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 caput 意为头。

normal.en: De- means off or away.
normal.cn: de- 意为去掉或离开。

normal.en: Decapitate means to take the head off.
normal.cn: decapitate 意为把头去掉。

normal.en: Capital and captain share the same head.
normal.cn: capital 与 captain 共享同一个「头」。

normal.en: Cut the top off a group and you decapitate it.
normal.cn: 把一个团体的顶层砍掉，就是 decapitate。

abstract.en: A blade falling and a head parting from a body.
abstract.cn: 一把刀落下，头与身体分开。

abstract.en: A tree whose top branch is cut away.
abstract.cn: 一棵被砍掉顶枝的树。

abstract.en: A body that keeps standing after the head is gone.
abstract.cn: 头没了、身体还站着的样子。

examples.en: The king was decapitated in the square.
examples.cn: 国王在广场上被斩首。

examples.en: The rebels decapitated the regime in one night.
examples.cn: 叛军一夜之间打掉了政权首脑。

examples.en: Decapitating the snake did not kill it at once.
examples.cn: 砍掉蛇头并没有让它立刻死去。

dict_mnemonic.text: de（去掉）＋ capit（头，像 captain 船长＝船上的头）＋ -ate（动词）＝ decapitate「去头」，即斩首。

root: 拉丁语 caput（头）＋ de-（去掉）→ decapitare（砍头）→ 英语 decapitate

sensesIntro.en: One blade: taking a head off, and taking the top off a group.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一把刀：砍下头颅，也砍掉一个团体的顶层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blade falling and the head parting from the body
core.cn: 核心意象：一把刀落下，头与身体分开

branches.en: A blade falling and a head parting from a body.
branches.cn: 一把刀落下，头与身体分开。

branches.en: A tree whose top branch is cut away.
branches.cn: 一棵被砍掉顶枝的树。

branches.en: Both take away the part that leads the rest.
branches.cn: 两者都拿走了带领其余部分的那一块。

branches.en: A body that keeps standing after the head is gone.
branches.cn: 头没了、身体还站着的样子。

branches.en: A group that goes on but has nobody to direct it.
branches.cn: 一个还在运转、却没人指挥的团体。

intro.en: Decapitate is de- plus caput; the head root builds capital and captain.
intro.cn: decapitate 由 de- 加 caput 构成；「头」这个词根造出 capital 与 captain。

latinIntro.en: Latin caput means head and caedere means to cut.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 caput 意为头，caedere 意为砍。

definition_en: to be slowly destroyed by natural processes
core_image: 木头上慢慢扩大的霉斑
scene: 雨漏了整年，屋梁一点点烂掉。The wooden beams had begun to decay.
sceneCN: 这里 decay 指「腐烂」（第 1 个义项：自然分解）；句意是木梁已经开始烂了。

senses.title: Rot away by natural process
senses.definition: to be broken down slowly by air, water or tiny living things
senses.definitionCN: 被空气、水或微生物慢慢分解
senses.example: The wooden beams had begun to decay.
senses.exampleCN: 木梁已经开始腐烂。
senses.why: Nothing is destroyed at once; small losses add up in the dark.
senses.whyCN: 没有东西是一下子坏掉的，细小的损耗在暗处累加。

senses.title: Lose strength or quality
senses.definition: to become weaker or worse in condition over time
senses.definitionCN: 随着时间变得衰弱或状况变差
senses.example: The old port decayed after the railway arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路修来之后，老港口衰落了。
senses.why: Buildings and towns age the same way fruit does.
senses.whyCN: 房屋和城镇变老的方式，和水果一样。

senses.title: The rotten part itself
senses.definition: the state or the visible result of having rotted
senses.definitionCN: 腐坏的状态，或看得见的腐坏结果
senses.example: The dentist found decay under the old filling.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医在旧补牙下面发现了蛀坏。
senses.why: The process leaves a trace that can be seen and named.
senses.whyCN: 这个过程会留下看得见、叫得出的痕迹。

intro.en: Decay came from Old French decair, from Latin decidere, to fall off, built on cadere, to fall.
intro.cn: decay 来自古法语 decair，源于拉丁语 decidere（脱落），根子是 cadere（落下）。

items.en: Decidere meant to fall away or drop off, like a leaf.
items.cn: decidere 指像叶子那样脱落。

items.en: The sense widened to wasting away and losing strength.
items.cn: 词义扩大到「耗损、失去力气」。

items.en: Decair meant to sink into a worse state.
items.cn: decair 指陷入更糟的状态。

items.en: Decay described bodies, wood and buildings losing their strength.
items.cn: decay 形容身体、木头和房屋失去支撑。

items.en: Physics gave decay a precise sense for unstable atoms.
items.cn: 物理学赋予它指不稳定原子衰变的精确含义。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one middle sound, and the meaning group moves from rot to collapse.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个中间音，近义组则从腐烂走到崩塌。

entries.definition: to make something happen later
a thing used to lead someone away
to give money back
to go bad and soft through natural change
entries.definitionCN: 因自然变化而变坏变软

entries.definition: to become unfit to eat
to break into small pieces slowly

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a damp beam and end with a town that lost its reason to exist.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一根受潮的屋梁开始，落到一座失去存在理由的城镇。

normal.en: Water finds the one board the builder forgot.
normal.cn: 水总能找到匠人漏掉的那块板。

normal.en: Decay is patient; it has no deadline.
normal.cn: 腐烂很有耐心，它没有期限。

normal.en: A tooth decays quietly until the night it does not.
normal.cn: 牙齿一直悄悄坏着，直到某个夜里突然疼起来。

normal.en: Ports die when the road goes somewhere else.
normal.cn: 路改了方向，港口就死了。

normal.en: The same slow falling is called decay in wood and in empires.
normal.cn: 木头和帝国身上那种缓慢的塌落，都叫 decay。

abstract.en: Picture a dark spot spreading on a painted wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一块深色斑在粉墙上慢慢扩大。

abstract.en: Picture a roof beam that gives way without a sound.
abstract.cn: 想象一根屋梁悄无声息地塌下来。

abstract.en: Picture an empty harbour with grass in the cracks.
abstract.cn: 想象一个空港口，石缝里长出了草。

examples.en: The wooden beams had begun to decay.
examples.cn: 木梁已经开始腐烂。

examples.en: Sugar feeds the bacteria that cause tooth decay.
examples.cn: 糖养活了导致蛀牙的细菌。

examples.en: The empire decayed from within long before it fell.
examples.cn: 这个帝国在崩塌之前早已从内部衰败。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 decay 记成「得开」：木头受了潮，纹理就一层层得开、裂开，最后整块烂掉。

root: 来自古法语 decair，源于拉丁语 decidere（脱落），根子是 cadere（落下），本义像叶子离枝。后来词义由「掉落」转为「耗损、失去力气」，十五世纪进入英语后用来形容木材、身体与建筑的朽坏，现代物理学又用它指原子衰变。

sensesIntro.en: From material rotting in the wet, to a town losing its strength, to the rot itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 从潮湿中烂掉的物质，到失去力气的城镇，再到那块烂掉的地方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark stain spreading slowly across wet wood.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块深色霉斑在湿木头上慢慢铺开。

branches.en: The first sense is the material itself coming apart.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是材料本身一点点散掉。

branches.en: The same slow loss, seen in a town or a system, becomes decline.
branches.cn: 同样的慢性损耗出现在城镇或制度上，就成了衰退。

branches.en: What is left behind can be seen, touched and named.
branches.cn: 留在原处的东西看得见、摸得着，也就能被称呼。

branches.en: The process and its trace are two views of one change.
branches.cn: 过程和痕迹，是同一场变化的两种看法。

branches.en: Decay in a thing and decay in a place look the same to the eye.
branches.cn: 东西上的朽坏和地方上的衰败，看上去是一回事。

intro.en: Decay has a thin family: the adjective of what has rotted, and the nouns of moral and cultural falling.
intro.cn: decay 这一族很薄：形容烂掉之物的形容词，还有指风气与文明堕落的名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is cadere, to fall; decidere meant to fall away from the whole.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 cadere（落下），decidere 指从整体上脱落。

items.exampleCN: 他们锯掉了烂掉的树枝。

items.example: A decaying wall stood at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 门口立着一堵正在朽坏的墙。
纸是一种会朽坏的材料。

items.example: Sweet drinks speed up tooth decay.

items.meaning: the breaking down of unstable atoms
the falling apart of a city area
items.example: The film shows urban decay in the old port.
items.exampleCN: 这部影片呈现了老港区的衰败。

items.example: Critics spoke of moral decay in the capital.
items.exampleCN: 批评者谈到首都的道德败坏。

latinEntries.example: Cadere gives English decay, cadence and accident.
latinEntries.exampleCN: cadere 为英语带来 decay、cadence 和 accident 这些词。

definition_en: to make someone believe something that is not true
core_image: 一只手在桌下悄悄换掉了牌
scene: 他嘴上说得漂亮，背后却换掉了账本。She did not mean to deceive anyone.
sceneCN: 这里 deceive 指「欺骗」（第 1 个义项：让人相信假的事）；句意是她并非有意骗人。

senses.title: Make someone believe a lie
senses.definition: to cause a person to accept something false as true
senses.definitionCN: 让一个人把假的当成真的接受下来
senses.example: She did not mean to deceive anyone.
senses.exampleCN: 她并不是有意骗谁。
senses.why: A lie only works when another mind takes it in.
senses.whyCN: 谎言只有在另一个脑子接收之后才算成立。

senses.title: Trick someone into acting
senses.definition: to lead a person by false words into doing something
senses.definitionCN: 用假话把某人引去做某件事
senses.example: He deceived the old man into signing the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 他骗老人签了那份文件。
senses.why: False words become a handle that turns another hand.
senses.whyCN: 假话成了一个把手，能转动别人的手。

senses.title: Cheat the eye
senses.definition: to give the senses a false impression
senses.definitionCN: 给感官一个不真实的印象
senses.example: The mirror deceives the eye and makes the room look wider.
senses.exampleCN: 镜子骗过眼睛，让房间显得更宽。
senses.why: What looks true can be built on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 看上去真的东西，也可能是特意做出来的。

intro.en: Deceive came from Old French deceivre, from Latin decipere, to catch in a trap, built on capere, to take.
intro.cn: deceive 来自古法语 deceivre，源于拉丁语 decipere（设套捕捉），根子是 capere（拿取）。

items.en: Decipere meant to catch something in a trap.
items.cn: decipere 指用套子把东西捉住。

items.en: The trap became a trick played on a person's mind.
items.cn: 网套变成了设在人心上的圈套。

items.en: Deceivre carried the sense of betraying trust.
items.cn: deceivre 带着背弃信任的意味。

items.en: Deceive entered English as both cheat and mislead.
items.cn: deceive 进入英语时兼指行骗与误导。

items.en: Deceive is now mostly about beliefs rather than property.
items.cn: 如今 deceive 多指骗人的认知，而不只是骗财物。

note.en: The look-alike group all end in the same sound, and the meaning group moves from small tricks to large fraud.
note.cn: 形近组收着同一个尾音，近义组则从小花招走到大诈骗。

entries.definition: to get something that is given or sent
entries.definitionCN: 收到别人给或寄来的东西

entries.definition: to form an idea in the mind
to notice or understand something
to act dishonestly to win or gain
entries.definitionCN: 为取胜或得利而做不诚实的事

entries.definition: to guide someone to a wrong belief
to fool someone for fun or gain
entries.definitionCN: 为了好玩或得利而捉弄人

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a card swapped under a table and end with a mirror that lies about the room.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从桌下被换掉的一张牌开始，落到一面谎报房间大小的镜子。

normal.en: A lie needs two people: one to speak it, one to believe it.
normal.cn: 谎言需要两个人：一个说，一个信。

normal.en: The surest liar first makes you trust him.
normal.cn: 最稳的骗子，先让你信任他。

normal.en: Nobody likes being deceived; everybody has deceived himself.
normal.cn: 没人喜欢被骗，可每个人都骗过自己。

normal.en: The eye is easiest to fool because it never asks questions.
normal.cn: 眼睛最容易骗，因为它从不提问。

normal.en: De- away, -ceive take: to be deceived is to be taken aside.
normal.cn: de 是离开，ceive 是拿取，被骗就是被人悄悄拿走。

abstract.en: Picture a hand under the table moving one card.
abstract.cn: 想象桌下一只手挪动了一张牌。

abstract.en: Picture a smile that is prepared before the question is asked.
abstract.cn: 想象一个在问题提出之前就准备好的微笑。

abstract.en: Picture a painted door that opens onto a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇画上去的门，推开却是墙。

examples.en: She did not mean to deceive anyone.
examples.cn: 她并不是有意骗谁。

examples.en: The advertisement deceived buyers about the size of the flat.
examples.cn: 广告在房子面积上骗了买家。

examples.en: Do not deceive yourself that the work is finished.
examples.cn: 别自欺欺人地以为活儿已经干完了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deceive 记成「递西服」：de 是递，ceive 像收，把一件假西服递过去让人收下，就是骗人。

root: 经古法语 deceivre 进入英语，源于拉丁语 decipere，本义是「设套捉住」，由 de（离开）与 capere（抓取）构成。捕兽的网套后来变成设在人心上的骗局，所以这个词从一开始就带着「套住」的意味。

sensesIntro.en: From making a mind accept a falsehood, to leading a hand into an act, to fooling the eye.
sensesIntro.cn: 从让一个脑子接受假话，到把一只手引进某个动作，再到骗过眼睛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a card swapped under the table while faces stay calm.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌下换掉一张牌，桌上的表情不变。

branches.en: The first sense is the false belief planted in another mind.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是种进别人脑子里的错误相信。

branches.en: The belief is then used to move the deceived person into action.
branches.cn: 这份相信随后被用来推动受骗的人去做事。

branches.en: The senses can be fooled without any belief at all.
branches.cn: 感官可以在没有任何相信的情况下被蒙住。

branches.en: False words first enter the mind, then leave it as a deed.
branches.cn: 假话先进脑子，再以行动的形式离开它。

branches.en: Both senses describe a false picture that produces a real result.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在说假画面造出了真结果。

intro.en: Deceive gathers its whole family: the act, the quality, the person, and the plainer noun deceit.
intro.cn: deceive 把整族都聚齐了：行为、性质、行骗的人，还有更朴素的 deceit。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is capere, to take or seize, with de- adding the sense of away.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 capere（抓取），前缀 de- 添上「拿走」的意味。

items.meaning: to make someone believe a lie

items.exampleCN: 那个骗子始终没被抓住。

items.example: He felt deceived by the letter.
items.exampleCN: 那封信让他觉得受了骗。

items.example: The contract was signed by deceit.
items.exampleCN: 这份合同是靠欺诈签下的。
这项任务看着简单，其实不然。

latinEntries.example: Capere gives English capture, receive and deceive.
latinEntries.exampleCN: capere 给英语带来 capture、receive 和 deceive。

definition_zh: v. 减速；减缓（增长、进程等）
definition_en: to become slower, or to make a vehicle or process slower
core_image: 脚从油门移到刹车上，速度表的指针往回走
scene: 司机在弯道前减速。The driver decelerated before the bend.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：decelerate 指车辆减速；句意是司机在弯道前减速。

senses.title: Slow a vehicle
senses.definition: to make a vehicle go more slowly
senses.definitionCN: 使车辆走得更慢
senses.example: The train decelerated into the station.
senses.exampleCN: 火车进站时减速。
senses.why: A foot moving from the accelerator to the brake.
senses.whyCN: 一只脚从油门移到刹车上。

senses.title: Slow a process
senses.definition: to make growth or progress happen more slowly
senses.definitionCN: 使增长或进展变慢
senses.example: Inflation decelerated last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年通胀放缓。
senses.why: A river that widens and therefore runs slower.
senses.whyCN: 一条变宽后流速变慢的河。

intro.en: Decelerate is de- plus accelerate: the reverse of speeding up.
intro.cn: decelerate 由 de- 加 accelerate 构成：加速的反向。

items.en: Celer meant swift.
items.cn: celer 意为快。

items.en: Accelerare meant to make swift.
items.cn: accelerare 意为使变快。

items.en: Accelerate entered English as to speed up.
items.cn: 十六世纪 accelerate 以「加速」义进入英语。

items.en: The prefix de- was used to reverse an action.
items.cn: 前缀 de- 用来表示反向动作。

items.en: Decelerate was formed to mean to slow down.
items.cn: 十九世纪 decelerate 被造出来表示减速。

items.en: Decelerate is used for economies and growth too.
items.cn: 二十世纪 decelerate 也用于经济与增长。

note.en: The look-alike group shares celer-; the near-meaning group names ways of going slower.
note.cn: 形近组共享 celer-；近义组都是「变慢」的说法。

entries.definition: To make something go faster.
The act or rate of slowing down.
The act or rate of speeding up.
Speed of movement.
To make or become slower.
To slow a vehicle with a brake.
To become less fast or less tight.
To make something happen later.

normalIntro.en: Decelerate is de- plus accelerate: take the speed away.
normalIntro.cn: decelerate 就是 de- 加 accelerate：把速度拿掉。

normal.en: Celer means swift in Latin.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 celer 意为快。

normal.en: Accelerate means to make swift.
normal.cn: accelerate 意为使变快。

normal.en: De- reverses the action.
normal.cn: de- 把动作反过来。

normal.en: Decelerate means to make slow.
normal.cn: decelerate 意为使变慢。

normal.en: Growth can decelerate as well as a car.
normal.cn: 增长和汽车一样可以 decelerate。

abstract.en: A foot moving from the accelerator to the brake.
abstract.cn: 一只脚从油门移到刹车上。

abstract.en: A river that widens and therefore runs slower.
abstract.cn: 一条变宽后流速变慢的河。

abstract.en: A needle on a dial walking backwards.
abstract.cn: 仪表盘上一根往回走的指针。

examples.en: The driver decelerated before the bend.
examples.cn: 司机在弯道前减速。

examples.en: Sales growth decelerated in the spring.
examples.cn: 春季销售增长放缓。

examples.en: The plane decelerates after it lands.
examples.cn: 飞机落地后减速。

dict_mnemonic.text: de（去掉）＋ celer（快，像 accelerate 加速）＋ -ate＝ decelerate「去快」，就是减速。

root: 拉丁语 celer（快）→ accelerare（使快）→ 英语 accelerate ＋ de-（反向）→ decelerate

sensesIntro.en: One needle walking back: a car slows, and so does growth.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一根往回走的指针：车会慢，增长也会慢。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot off the accelerator and a needle walking back
core.cn: 核心意象：脚离开油门，指针往回走

branches.en: A foot moving from the accelerator to the brake.
branches.cn: 一只脚从油门移到刹车上。

branches.en: A river that widens and therefore runs slower.
branches.cn: 一条变宽后流速变慢的河。

branches.en: Both are the same needle walking backwards.
branches.cn: 两者都是同一根往回走的指针。

branches.en: A needle on a dial walking backwards.
branches.cn: 仪表盘上一根往回走的指针。

branches.en: A curve that keeps rising but rises less steeply.
branches.cn: 一条仍在上升、却升得越来越平的曲线。

intro.en: Decelerate is de- plus accelerate; the swift root also builds celerity.
intro.cn: decelerate 由 de- 加 accelerate 构成；「快」这个词根也造出 celerity。

latinIntro.en: Latin celer means swift and tardus means slow.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 celer 意为快，tardus 意为慢。

definition_en: of a good enough standard; honest and kind
core_image: 一件洗得干净、不新却合身的衬衫
scene: 他穿着干净的旧衬衫去面试，看着让人放心。He is a decent man who keeps his word.
sceneCN: 这里 decent 指「正派的」（第 3 个义项：为人端正）；句意他是个守信的正派人。

senses.title: Good enough in quality
senses.definition: acceptable in quality, though not excellent
senses.definitionCN: 质量可以接受，虽不算出色
senses.example: He finally found a decent job near home.
senses.exampleCN: 他终于在离家不远的地方找到一份像样的工作。
senses.why: A low bar is still a bar; decent marks the line above it.
senses.whyCN: 低的标准也是标准，decent 指的就是这条线以上。

senses.title: Proper and respectable
senses.definition: following accepted standards of dress or behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 符合大家认可的穿着与举止标准
senses.example: Wear something decent to the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 面试时穿得体面一点。
senses.why: What is proper is decided by the eyes of other people.
senses.whyCN: 什么叫得体，是由别人的眼睛定的。

senses.title: Honest and kind
senses.definition: having good moral qualities
senses.definitionCN: 具备良好的品德
senses.example: He is a decent man who keeps his word.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个守信的正派人。
senses.why: The word turns from manners to morals without changing shape.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从礼貌转到品行，外形一点没变。

intro.en: Decent came from Latin decens, fitting or becoming, from decere, to be proper.
intro.cn: decent 来自拉丁语 decens（合适的、相称的），源于 decere（应当、合宜）。

items.en: Decere meant to be fitting or proper for someone.
items.cn: decere 指对某人来说是合宜的。

items.en: Decens described what suits a person's place and duty.
items.cn: decens 形容与身份和职责相称的东西。

items.en: Décent carried the sense of proper and modest.
items.cn: décent 带着得体、有分寸的意思。

items.en: Decent named behaviour that met the standards of the day.
items.cn: decent 指符合当时标准的行为。

items.en: It softened into good enough, as in a decent meal.
items.cn: 后来它软化成「过得去」，比如一顿还不错的饭。

note.en: The look-alike group sounds close but means something else, and the meaning group runs from proper to merely acceptable.
note.cn: 形近组听着相近却另有意思，近义组则从得体走到勉强可以。

entries.definition: a movement downward
happening a short time ago
to pour liquid into another container
entries.definitionCN: 把液体倒进另一个容器

entries.definition: considered proper by other people
correct for the situation
not too large or showy

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a clean old shirt and end with the quiet honesty behind it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一件干净的旧衬衫开始，落到衬衫背后的那份老实。

normal.en: A decent shirt is not new; it is clean and fits.
normal.cn: 体面的衬衫不必新，干净合身就行。

normal.en: Decent is the word for the middle, where most of life happens.
normal.cn: decent 是给中间地带用的词，而生活大多在那儿。

normal.en: Pay a decent wage and the work becomes decent too.
normal.cn: 给一份说得过去的工钱，活儿也跟着像样了。

normal.en: A decent man does the right thing when nobody is watching.
normal.cn: 正派的人，在没人看着时也做该做的事。

normal.en: One letter turns decent into descent, and the meaning falls away.
normal.cn: 换一个字母，decent 就成了 descent，意思一落千丈。

abstract.en: Picture a shirt ironed on a kitchen table.
abstract.cn: 想象一件在厨房桌上被熨平的衬衫。

abstract.en: Picture a meal that is plain, warm and enough.
abstract.cn: 想象一顿简单、热乎、吃得饱的饭。

abstract.en: Picture a man returning money he was never asked about.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人把没人追问的钱还了回去。

examples.en: He is a decent man who keeps his word.
examples.cn: 他是个守信的正派人。

examples.en: She earns a decent salary and saves a little each month.
examples.cn: 她挣着一份不错的工资，每月还能存下一点。

examples.en: It was decent of you to wait for me.
examples.cn: 你等着我，真是厚道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 decent 记成「得体身」：de 是得，cent 听起来像「身」，衣着得体、为人端正，就是得体身。

root: 来自拉丁语 decens（合宜的），源于 decere（应当如此），本义是「与身份相称」。经法语 décent 进入英语后先指合乎礼俗的举止，后来语气变软，日常里常表示「还过得去、像样」。

sensesIntro.en: From something acceptable, to something proper in others' eyes, to a person worth trusting.
sensesIntro.cn: 从还算可以的东西，到别人眼里得体的样子，再到值得信任的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clean, plain shirt that fits exactly.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件干净朴素、正好合身的衬衫。

branches.en: The first sense only asks that a thing be acceptable.
branches.cn: 第一个义项只要求东西过得去。

branches.en: The second sense adds the eyes of other people.
branches.cn: 第二个义项添上了旁人的目光。

branches.en: The third moves from appearance to the person behind it.
branches.cn: 第三个义项从外表走到了外表背后的那个人。

branches.en: Quality and propriety both rest on a shared minimum.
branches.cn: 质量和得体，都靠一条大家公认的底线。

branches.en: Good manners and good morals are neighbours in this word.
branches.cn: 在这个词里，礼貌与品德是邻居。

intro.en: Decent pairs with its negative and its noun: decency, indecent, indecency.
intro.cn: decent 与否定形式和名词配对：decency、indecent、indecency。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is decere, to be fitting; decus gave the related idea of honour.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 decere（合宜），decus 则带来「荣誉、体面」的意思。

items.example: They live in a decent flat.
items.exampleCN: 他们住在一套还不错的公寓里。

items.example: He had the decency to apologise.
The sign was removed as indecent.
items.exampleCN: 那块招牌因不雅被拆掉了。

items.example: The court heard a charge of indecency.
items.exampleCN: 法庭审理了一项猥亵指控。

items.example: He was indecently dressed for the ceremony.
items.exampleCN: 他穿得不宜出席那个仪式。
他们找到一家看上去还像样的旅馆。

items.example: The flat has a decent-sized kitchen.
items.exampleCN: 这套公寓有个相当大的厨房。

latinEntries.example: Decere lies behind decent and decorum.
latinEntries.exampleCN: decere 是 decent 和 decorum 的来源。

definition_en: the act of making someone believe something untrue
core_image: 幕布后面那只操纵的手
scene: 观众以为箱子是空的，其实底下有夹层。The trick depends on simple deception.
sceneCN: 这里 deception 指「欺骗」（第 1 个义项：使人相信假象的行为）；句意是这戏法靠的是简单的骗术。

senses.title: The act of deceiving
senses.definition: the act of making a person believe what is false
senses.definitionCN: 让人相信不实之事的行为
senses.example: The trick depends on simple deception.
senses.exampleCN: 这个戏法靠的是简单的骗术。
senses.why: An act needs a doer and someone who is taken in.
senses.whyCN: 一个行为需要一个做的人，也需要一个上当的人。

senses.title: A false appearance
senses.definition: something that looks like one thing but is another
senses.definitionCN: 看着像一种东西，实际却是另一种
senses.example: The calm surface was a deception; the river ran fast.
senses.exampleCN: 平静的水面是个假象，河底流得很急。
senses.why: The world itself can wear a mask.
senses.whyCN: 世界本身也会戴上一张面具。

senses.title: The state of being fooled
senses.definition: the condition of having been taken in
senses.definitionCN: 已经上当之后的处境
senses.example: His trust made the deception harder to bear.
senses.exampleCN: 他的信任让这次受骗更难承受。
senses.why: The same event looks different from the other side.
senses.whyCN: 同一件事，从另一边看，样子完全不同。

intro.en: Deception is the Latin noun deceptio, from decipere, to catch in a trap.
intro.cn: deception 就是拉丁名词 deceptio，来自 decipere（设套捕捉）。

items.en: Deceptio named the act of catching someone in a trap.
items.cn: deceptio 指把人套住的行为。

items.en: The trap became a trick of words and appearances.
items.cn: 捕兽的套子变成了言语与外表上的圈套。

items.en: Déception meant a betrayal of trust.
items.cn: déception 指对信任的背弃。

items.en: Deception entered English as the noun of deceive.
items.cn: deception 作为 deceive 的名词进入英语。

items.en: It now covers lies, disguises and optical tricks.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖谎言、伪装与视觉把戏。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ception ending, and the meaning group names kinds of dishonesty.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -ception 结尾，近义组则列出各种不诚实。

entries.definition: the desk where visitors are received
the forming of an idea
a case that does not follow the rule
the crime of gaining money by lying
entries.definitionCN: 靠说谎获取钱财的犯罪

entries.definition: the use of clever tricks
a false picture seen by the senses

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a false bottom in a box and end with a trust that cannot be rebuilt.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从箱子里的夹层开始，落到一份再也修不好的信任。

normal.en: A magician never lies; he only lets you finish the story wrong.
normal.cn: 魔术师从不撒谎，他只是让你把故事想错。

normal.en: Deception needs an audience that is sure of itself.
normal.cn: 欺骗需要一个自以为看明白了的观众。

normal.en: The smoothest surface hides the fastest water.
normal.cn: 最平的水面，底下藏着最急的流。

normal.en: A false bottom makes a light box feel heavy.
normal.cn: 一个夹层，能让轻箱子摸起来很沉。

normal.en: Every deception costs two people: the fooled and the fooler.
normal.cn: 每场欺骗都要两个人付账：被骗的和骗人的。

abstract.en: Picture a curtain with a hand moving behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一道幕布，后面有一只手在动。

abstract.en: Picture a mirror placed to show a door that is not there.
abstract.cn: 想象一面镜子，照出一扇并不存在的门。

abstract.en: Picture a letter rewritten in the same handwriting.
abstract.cn: 想象一封用同样笔迹重写过的信。

examples.en: The trick depends on simple deception.
examples.cn: 这个戏法靠的是简单的骗术。

examples.en: He obtained the money by deception.
examples.cn: 他靠欺骗得到了这笔钱。

examples.en: Her calm voice hid the deception well.
examples.cn: 她平静的嗓音把骗局掩藏得很好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deception 记成「得塞不逊」：de 是得，ception 听着像「塞不逊」，把假话塞进别人耳朵，还说得头头是道。

root: 直接借自拉丁名词 deceptio，源头是 decipere（设套捉住），由 de（离开）与 capere（抓取）组成。词义从捕兽的网套一路扩展为言语上的骗局、外表上的假象，以及受骗之后的处境。

sensesIntro.en: From an act done by someone, to a false face worn by the world, to the state of the fooled.
sensesIntro.cn: 从某人做出的一次行为，到世界戴上的一张假脸，再到上当者的处境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand working behind a curtain.
core.cn: 核心意象：幕布后面有一只手在操作。

branches.en: The first sense is the act of putting the mask in place.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把面具戴上去的那个动作。

branches.en: The second sense is the mask itself, worn by a thing or a place.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是面具本身，戴在某物或某地脸上。

branches.en: The third sense is what it feels like once the mask falls.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是面具掉下来之后的感受。

branches.en: The act and the false face are the same trick seen twice.
branches.cn: 行为和假脸，是同一个把戏的两次呈现。

branches.en: One person's act becomes another person's injury.
branches.cn: 一个人的动作，变成另一个人的伤。

intro.en: Deception sits at the centre of a family built on the same Latin stem, cept-.
intro.cn: deception 位于一族词的中心，它们共用一个拉丁词干 cept-。

latinIntro.en: The stem is capere, to take, with its participle form captus and the derived cept-.
latinIntro.cn: 词干来自 capere（拿取），分词形式是 captus，由此派生出 cept-。

items.example: The whole scheme rested on deception.
items.exampleCN: 整个方案都建立在欺骗之上。
这条路看着窄，其实不然。

items.example: The deceptiveness of the map cost them an hour.
items.exampleCN: 地图的误导让他们多花了一小时。

items.example: His optimism was a form of self-deception.
The staff rehearsed the deception plan.
items.exampleCN: 工作人员演练了那套欺骗计划。

items.example: The team studied old deception tactics.
items.exampleCN: 小组研究了过去的欺骗战术。
他们对军官进行了反欺骗训练。

definition_zh: n. 分贝（声级或功率比的单位）
definition_en: a unit for measuring the level of a sound, or the ratio of two powers
core_image: 一格一格的音量条，每往上十格就翻一倍
scene: 工地噪声到了九十分贝。The noise on the site reached ninety decibels.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：decibel 指声级单位；句意是工地噪声达到九十分贝。

senses.title: Unit of sound level
senses.definition: a unit that tells how loud a sound is
senses.definitionCN: 表示声音有多响的单位
senses.example: The alarm reached ninety decibels.
senses.exampleCN: 警报声达到九十分贝。
senses.why: A bar of volume steps climbing one by one.
senses.whyCN: 一格一格往上爬的音量条。

senses.title: Unit of power ratio
senses.definition: a unit for the ratio between two signal powers
senses.definitionCN: 两个信号功率之比的单位
senses.example: The gain is three decibels.
senses.exampleCN: 增益是三分贝。
senses.why: A dial that compares two signals.
senses.whyCN: 一个比较两路信号的刻度盘。

intro.en: Decibel is deci- tenth plus bel, a unit named after Bell.
intro.cn: decibel 由 deci-（十分之一）加 bel 构成，bel 以贝尔命名。

items.en: Decimus meant tenth.
items.cn: decimus 意为第十。

items.en: Deci- meant one tenth.
items.cn: deci- 意为十分之一。

items.en: The bel was named after Alexander Graham Bell.
items.cn: 贝尔这个单位以亚历山大·格雷厄姆·贝尔命名。

items.en: The decibel was one tenth of a bel.
items.cn: 分贝是贝尔的十分之一。

items.en: Decibels became the standard unit for sound level.
items.cn: 分贝成为声级的标准单位。

items.en: Decibels are used in audio and telecom work.
items.cn: 分贝用于音频与电信工作。

note.en: The look-alike group shares deci-; the near-meaning group names other measures of sound.
note.cn: 形近组共享 deci-；近义组都是声音的其他度量。

A period of ten years.
One of ten equal parts of a set.
A unit of power ratio, ten decibels.
